The post Sapphire Surface Modification Enables Wafer-Scale 2D Semiconductor Growth (Peking U., CAS et al.) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: A research team from Peking University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences has developed a homo-metal-element surface modification strategy for sapphire substrates.

backlog.title: Research Bits: Sept. 1
backlog.summary:
Gallium nitride: High voltage; low resistance; diamond interposer.
The post Research Bits: Sept. 1 appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: EPFL researchers developed an intrinsic polarization superjunction (iPSJ) GaN transistor on silicon that achieves a record 4kV breakdown voltage while maintaining low resistance.
The iPSJ design avoids charge imbalance by balancing positive and electron charge sheets, eliminating the need for traditional chemical doping and improving reliability under high-temperature stress.
A separate research collaboration achieved a breakthrough in p-type GaN contact resistivity, reaching (1–3) × 10⁻⁴ Ω cm² by depositing an ultrathin magnesium layer and annealing at 600°C.
These advancements in GaN technology are critical for improving the efficiency and thermal robustness of next-generation power electronics, particularly for electric vehicles and industrial systems.

bullets: Virtual power plants (VPPs) aggregate household energy devices to balance grid demand, with smart thermostat programs offering $50–$150 bonuses and home battery systems yielding significantly higher annual savings.

bullets: Stanford and SLAC researchers introduced a deep learning approach to automate the extraction of physical parameters for 2D transistors.
The method uses a secondary neural network to approximate physics-based device simulators, streamlining TCAD fitting and electrical measurement analysis.
This automation reduces the manual effort required for device characterization, potentially speeding up the R&D pipeline for emerging 2D transistor technologies.

The post Programmable Silicon Photonics Filter Enables Continuous Laser Wavelength Tuning (UiT, Stanford) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Researchers from UiT and Stanford have demonstrated a programmable silicon photonic filter that enables continuous wavelength tuning for laser systems.
The device utilizes a forward-only interferometer mesh combined with a waveguide delay line array to achieve robust, nonresonant filtering.
This programmable approach offers a scalable method for controlling laser ring cavities, with potential applications in integrated optical communications and sensing.

backlog.title: How engineered microbes could help feed the world’s crops
backlog.summary: Fertilizer is crucial for the global food supply, but making it uses a lot of energy and produces a lot of emissions. Some companies hope microbes can help. A growing body of research shows that seeding the soil around a crop’s roots with beneficial microbes can help feed the plant, providing crucial nitrogen to help…
bullets: Switch Bioworks is developing a microbial fertilizer that uses a genetic switch to allow colonies to establish themselves before activating nitrogen-fixation processes.
Synthetic fertilizer production currently accounts for approximately 2% of global greenhouse gas emissions, creating significant market demand for sustainable biological alternatives.
The company aims to mitigate the 'energy cost' problem inherent in microbial nitrogen fixation, where ammonia production typically hinders the growth of the microbes themselves.

Rising fertilizer prices, exacerbated by geopolitical instability, are accelerating the commercial interest in biological soil additives as a cost-effective alternative to Haber-Bosch process products.

backlog.title: Facilitating AI integration with simplicity at scale
backlog.summary: As companies scale, the technology supporting operations can become a liability just as quickly as it becomes an asset. Disconnected systems, site-specific tools, spreadsheets, and manual workarounds can create data silos that make it harder to spot problems early, coordinate responses, and make decisions with confidence. For Jabil, a global manufacturing company with more than…
bullets: Jabil, a global manufacturer with over 100 sites, is prioritizing a 'simplify-first' strategy to establish a consistent data backbone before scaling AI initiatives.
The company emphasizes that innovation without process standardization creates technical debt and operational complexity rather than measurable business value.
Integration efforts focus on breaking down data silos across diverse regional workflows to enable real-time supply chain visibility and automated decision-making.
The strategy highlights that successful enterprise AI deployment is contingent upon seamless data flow, requiring significant governance and process maturity improvements.

backlog.title: Molecular Dynamics Study Explains Aluminum Dopant Activation In 4H-SiC (TU Wien, Silvaco)
backlog.summary:
Researchers from TU Wien and Silvaco Europe published a technical paper titled “The influence of implantation conditions on dopant activation in Al-implanted 4H-SiC: A MD study applying an Al potential fitted to DFT barriers.” Abstract Excerpt: “The non-monotonic dependence of Al dopant activation on implantation temperature in 4H-SiC has been experimentally observed but its atomistic... » read more
The post Molecular Dynamics Study Explains Aluminum Dopant Activation In 4H-SiC (TU Wien, Silvaco) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: A joint study by TU Wien and Silvaco uses molecular dynamics to clarify the atomistic origins of non-monotonic aluminum dopant activation in 4H-SiC.
The research models implantation temperatures of 500 K and 900 K across seven different dose levels to track defect formation and evolution.
These findings provide critical insights into early-stage annealing processes, helping to optimize manufacturing parameters for silicon carbide power semiconductors.

bullets: We trust designers to do the best they can, but know they cannot be perfect.
That’s why we verify.
When AI gets involved, it cannot be trusted.
We have to thank the Russians for the expression, ‘trust but verify’ (doveryai, no proveryai).
Suzanne Massie, a scholar of Russian history, taught it to Ronald Reagan while he was president.

backlog.title: How AI plotted an interstellar journey to Alpha Centauri
backlog.summary: A nonprofit organization called the Fermi Explorer Mission announced today that it intends to launch a spacecraft to our nearest star system by the end of 2029.  It’s a hugely ambitious mission—if all goes well, the spacecraft could take up to 80,000 years to arrive at Alpha Centauri, which is 4.4 light-years away. And the…
bullets: The Fermi Explorer Mission plans a 2029 launch to Alpha Centauri using a trajectory optimized by an AI system developed by Physical Superintelligence (PSI).
The mission is backed by $58 million in funding from Breakthrough Energy, though the specific interstellar probe project is operating on a lean $15 million budget.
Unlike previous high-speed proposals, this mission prioritizes feasibility over speed, accepting a potential transit time of up to 80,000 years to reach the star system.
The spacecraft will carry a one-kilogram payload, including scientific instruments and a modern iteration of the Golden Record.

backlog.title: Agriculture relies on fossil fuels. It’s costing us.
backlog.summary: If you’ve had to fill up your vehicle’s gas tank or buy a plane ticket lately, you’ve probably felt the effects of rising fossil-fuel prices. But farmers buying fertilizer for their crops are especially aware of just how far the ripple effects of the conflict in Iran have spread. Fertilizer prices have been on a…
bullets: Fertilizer production is deeply tied to fossil fuel markets, as natural gas serves as both an energy source and a primary chemical feedstock for ammonia.
The conflict in Iran has disrupted the Strait of Hormuz, a critical transit route for one-third of global seaborne fertilizer trade, exacerbating price volatility.
Urea prices reached $850 per metric ton in April, an 80% increase compared to pre-conflict levels, highlighting the vulnerability of agricultural inputs to geopolitical instability.
Fertilizer manufacturing accounts for approximately 2% of global greenhouse gas emissions, prompting increased interest in climate-friendly alternatives like genetically edited microbes.

backlog.title: Protecting Mission-Critical Data Beyond The SoC: Why Inline Memory Encryption Needs Integrity
backlog.summary:
Aerospace and government systems need confidentiality, authentication, and implementation resilience for off-chip memory.
The post Protecting Mission-Critical Data Beyond The SoC: Why Inline Memory Encryption Needs Integrity appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Inline Memory Encryption (IME) is essential for protecting sensitive data as it moves between the SoC and off-chip memory, a critical attack surface.
Encryption alone is insufficient for mission-critical systems because it does not prevent attackers from altering data, which can lead to system-level manipulation.
Security architects must implement authentication alongside encryption to ensure data integrity, particularly for AI models where poisoned inputs can compromise inference results.

backlog.title: Building Trust Into Physical AI Systems
backlog.summary:
Security and safety are inseparable in the physical world.
The post Building Trust Into Physical AI Systems appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Physical AI systems, such as autonomous vehicles and industrial robots, require higher reliability standards because errors can lead to direct physical harm.
Security vulnerabilities in physical AI extend beyond software to include training data bias and sensor spoofing, which can degrade perception and decision-making.
Trust in physical AI must be built across the entire chain, from initial data ingestion and sensor input to the final physical actuation.

backlog.title: Humanoid Compute, Security More Complex Than AVs
backlog.summary:
Robots and autonomous vehicles are both edge devices, but a humanoid has wheels as well as fingers. Close interaction with humans raises the stakes. 
The post Humanoid Compute, Security More Complex Than AVs appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: The U.S. robotics market reached $11.4 billion in 2026, with humanoid development increasingly relying on AI-native architectures rather than retrofitted hardware.
Humanoid compute architectures are evolving into hybrid models, featuring a central AI unit for high-level planning and zonal microcontrollers for real-time, safety-critical actuation.
Safety in humanoid robotics requires a certified hardware-based 'safety companion' that operates independently of the AI model to ensure fault tolerance.

backlog.title: What Can Go Wrong In 800VDC AI Data Centers
backlog.summary:
Sparks and fires caused by higher electrical currents can cause costly outages and put people in danger. Hot chips also cause problems. 
The post What Can Go Wrong In 800VDC AI Data Centers appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Data centers are transitioning to 800V DC power distribution to support high-density AI racks, which can reach 1 megawatt per rack.
Higher voltages improve efficiency and thermal performance through wide bandgap semiconductors like GaN, but they significantly increase the risk of dangerous power arcs during hot-swapping.
Reliability in 800V environments requires advanced isolation and protective hot-swap circuitry to prevent catastrophic equipment failure and ensure worker safety.

backlog.title: How Many Design Experiments Does A Machine Learning Predictor Actually Need?
backlog.summary:
Required dataset size and achievable accuracy track how smooth the response is, not model size or number of design variables. 
The post How Many Design Experiments Does A Machine Learning Predictor Actually Need? appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: The number of experiments required to train an ML predictor in CAE is determined by the smoothness of the response function rather than the number of design variables.
Discontinuous responses, such as integer counts of damaged battery cells, require significantly larger datasets to achieve predictive accuracy compared to smooth functions like mass.
Engineers should prioritize the nature of the physical response when planning simulation budgets, as model size does not correlate with the training data requirements.
